title: Fire, Track, Review
one_liner: Review the artifact, not the agent. Dispatch the task, track the output, inspect the result.
problem: Watching an agent work feels productive and creates a sense of control, but it consumes the same scarce resource agents are supposed to save: human attention. Continuous supervision pulls the operator down to the execution layer — interrupting, second-guessing, and reacting to intermediate steps — instead of staying at the meta level where tasks, priorities and outcomes are decided. Busy is not the same as in control.
solution: Use agents like asynchronous workers, not stage performers. Dispatch a clear task with a defined expected output. The agent works in a bounded environment and produces a reviewable artifact — branch, diff, pull request, draft, report — backed by automated checks, a written summary, risk notes and any follow-up tasks. Sentinels and automated review pull human attention only when the result needs it. At the review point, inspect the artifact or diff, tests and evidence summary; open the chat or tool trace only when evidence is missing or the outcome is suspicious. Human attention is spent at review points, not during the agent's working phase. Calibration runs are the explicit exception: watch enough to improve the system, not to feel in control.
